newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50- trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50- trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen mostly steady to up $0.50 per cwt, depending on marketings, livestock dealers said.

In areas of Iowa and southern Minnesota where rainfall delayed harvesting and left producers free to move hogs, Tuesday's marketings met demand and even gave some packers enough inventory to get through Wednesday and into early Thursday, sources there said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in the interior Iowa/southern Minnesota area could range from $52.00 to $53.00, steady with Tuesday, sources said.
Illinois hog prices at plants were called steady Wednesday and could range from $51.00 to $51.50.
Indiana/Ohio top prices were seen up $0.50 amid light marketings, with a top plant price of $50.50 to $51.50, possibly $51.75, sources in those areas said.
Demand for the hogs reportedly was fueled by strengthening pork cutout values and moderate pork demand, sources said.

Carlot pork prices at midday were quoted mixed on 42.0 loads of pork reported sold and 21.0 loads of trimmings, USDA said. Loins were untested and hams were steady to weak while seedless bellies were quoted $1.00 higher.
However, some sources expected values to firm by the close.
